polities.name: Caral-Supe
polities.blurb: The oldest known urban civilisation in the Americas, building monumental platform mounds on the Peruvian coast while the pyramids rose in Egypt.

polities.name: Poverty Point Culture
polities.blurb: A network of earthwork-building communities in the lower Mississippi valley, centred on one of the largest mound complexes of its age.

polities.name: Olmec Civilisation
polities.blurb: Mesoamerica's first major civilisation, remembered for colossal stone heads and for patterns of kingship and calendar-keeping that later cultures inherited.

polities.name: Maya Civilisation
polities.blurb: A civilisation of rival city-states with a full writing system and precise astronomy. The classic cities collapsed around 900 CE but Maya kingdoms lasted until the Spanish conquest.

polities.name: Chavín Culture
polities.blurb: A religious and artistic tradition radiating from the temple complex of Chavín de Huántar across the central Andes.

polities.name: Zapotec Civilisation
polities.blurb: Builders of Monte Albán in Oaxaca, with one of the earliest writing systems in the Americas.

polities.name: Teotihuacan
polities.blurb: For centuries the largest city in the Americas, its Pyramid of the Sun anchoring an influence that reached deep into Maya country.

polities.name: Moche & Nazca
polities.blurb: Coastal Peruvian cultures known for irrigation, portrait pottery and the desert lines.

polities.name: Tiwanaku
polities.blurb: A polity centred on the high shores of Lake Titicaca whose stone architecture and llama caravans tied the southern Andes together.

polities.name: Wari Empire
polities.blurb: An Andean highland empire of roads and colonies that prefigured Inca administration.

polities.name: Mississippian Culture
polities.blurb: Mound-building chiefdoms across the American Southeast and Midwest. Cahokia, near modern St Louis, was larger than contemporary London.

polities.name: Toltec
polities.blurb: A central Mexican power the Aztecs claimed as their prestigious ancestors.

polities.name: Chimú Kingdom
polities.blurb: The Inca's largest rival, whose adobe capital was the biggest mud-brick city in the Americas.

polities.name: Aztec Empire
polities.blurb: The Triple Alliance that dominated central Mexico from the island city of Tenochtitlan, felled by Cortés and his native allies.

polities.name: Inca Empire
polities.blurb: The largest empire of the pre-Columbian Americas, running the length of the Andes on a road network without wheels or writing.

polities.name: Haudenosaunee Confederacy
polities.blurb: The Iroquois League of five, later six, nations, whose council governed the eastern woodlands for centuries.

polities.name: Brazil
polities.blurb: Portuguese colony, then the only monarchy in the Americas, then the continent's largest republic.

polities.name: New Spain
polities.blurb: The Spanish viceroyalty built on the ruins of the Aztec world, shipping American silver into the first truly global economy.

polities.name: United States
polities.blurb: The federal republic born of thirteen British colonies, an industrial and then global power by the twentieth century.

polities.name: Argentina & Chile
polities.blurb: Southern Cone republics that won independence together under San Martín.

polities.name: Gran Colombia & Andean Republics
polities.blurb: Bolívar's union broke into Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia within a decade.

polities.name: Mexico
polities.blurb: Independent from Spain in 1821, reshaped by revolution a century later.

polities.name: Canada
polities.blurb: A confederation of British North American colonies, bilingual from the start.

polities.name: Andronovo Culture
polities.blurb: Bronze Age herders of the western steppe, likely speakers of Indo-Iranian languages ancestral to Persian and Sanskrit.

polities.name: Scythians
polities.blurb: Nomad horse-archers of the Pontic and Central Asian steppe, famous for gold animal art and for defeating every army sent after them.

polities.name: Xiongnu Empire
polities.blurb: The first great steppe confederation, whose pressure on Han China shaped the Great Wall and the Silk Road alike.

polities.name: Kushan Empire
polities.blurb: A Central Asian empire spanning Bactria and northern India, a crossroads state that carried Buddhism toward China.

polities.name: Göktürk Khaganate
polities.blurb: The first empire to rule the steppe under the Turkic name, leaving the oldest written Turkic monuments on the Orkhon.

polities.name: Khazar Khaganate
polities.blurb: A steppe empire between Byzantium and the caliphate whose elite converted to Judaism.

polities.name: Uyghur Khaganate
polities.blurb: The Turkic empire that succeeded the Göktürks and propped up the Tang during the An Lushan rebellion.

polities.name: Samanid Empire
polities.blurb: The Persian revival in Central Asia, where Bukhara's libraries trained Avicenna and New Persian literature began.

polities.name: Cumans & Pechenegs
polities.blurb: Turkic nomad confederations of the Pontic steppe, scattered by the Mongol advance.

polities.name: Ghaznavid Empire
polities.blurb: Turkic slave-soldiers turned emperors, whose raids opened northern India to Muslim rule.

polities.name: Khwarazmian Empire
polities.blurb: A Persianate empire of Central Asia and Iran whose execution of Mongol envoys invited the most devastating invasion of the age.

polities.name: Qara Khitai
polities.blurb: Liao refugees who rebuilt an empire in Central Asia and reached Europe as the legend of Prester John.

polities.name: Mongol Empire
polities.blurb: Genghis Khan's empire became the largest contiguous one in history, linking China to Europe under a single peace and a single postal relay.

polities.name: Golden Horde
polities.blurb: The Mongol khanate of the western steppe, overlord of the Russian principalities for over two centuries.

polities.name: Timurid Empire
polities.blurb: Timur's conquests rebuilt a Mongol-scale empire with Persian high culture; his descendants made Samarkand and Herat brilliant.

polities.name: Kazakh Khanate
polities.blurb: The steppe khanate whose three hordes defined Kazakh identity before absorption into the Russian Empire.

polities.name: Khanates of Bukhara & Khiva
polities.blurb: Uzbek successor states along the Silk Road oases, absorbed by Russia in the nineteenth century.

polities.name: Dzungar Khanate
polities.blurb: The last steppe empire, destroyed by the Qing in a campaign that emptied the Ili valley.

polities.name: Kazakhstan
polities.blurb: The largest of the post-Soviet Central Asian republics, spanning the old steppe heartland.

polities.name: Xia / Erlitou
polities.blurb: The bronze-working Erlitou culture on the Yellow River, identified by many with the semi-legendary Xia dynasty.

polities.name: Shang Dynasty
polities.blurb: China's first historical dynasty, whose oracle-bone inscriptions are the earliest Chinese writing.

polities.name: Western Zhou
polities.blurb: The dynasty of the Mandate of Heaven, parcelling the realm among kin in a pattern later ages idealised.

polities.name: Eastern Zhou
polities.blurb: Five centuries of a nominal king and warring states, and simultaneously the age of Confucius, Laozi and the hundred schools.

polities.name: Qin Dynasty
polities.blurb: The brief, ferocious unification: one script, one currency, one emperor, and the terracotta army guarding his tomb.

polities.name: Han Dynasty
polities.blurb: The dynasty that fixed the template of the Chinese imperial state, contemporary with Rome and connected to it by the Silk Road.

polities.name: Three Kingdoms
polities.blurb: Wei, Shu and Wu divided the Han inheritance, a brief era that became China's most retold story.

polities.name: Jin Dynasty
polities.blurb: A short reunification after the Three Kingdoms, then a court in exile south of the Yangtze as the north fragmented.

polities.name: Sixteen Kingdoms
polities.blurb: Northern China fragmented among short-lived states founded largely by steppe peoples.

polities.name: Northern & Southern Dynasties
polities.blurb: China split along the Yangtze for a century and a half, the north under Xianbei rulers, the south under exiled Han courts.

polities.name: Sui Dynasty
polities.blurb: Reunified China after four centuries of division and dug the Grand Canal, exhausting itself in the process.

polities.name: Tang Dynasty
polities.blurb: A cosmopolitan high point of imperial China, its capital the largest city on earth and its poetry still memorised today.

polities.name: Tibetan Empire
polities.blurb: From the Himalayan plateau Tibet contested Central Asia with Tang China and briefly took its capital.

polities.name: Nanzhao & Dali
polities.blurb: Successive kingdoms in Yunnan that held off Tang armies and traded between China, Tibet and Burma.

polities.name: Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms
polities.blurb: Five northern dynasties and ten southern states filled the seventy years between Tang and Song.

polities.name: Liao Dynasty
polities.blurb: The Khitan empire of the northern steppe and north China, whose name became the Russian word for China.

polities.name: Song Dynasty
polities.blurb: Paper money, printing, gunpowder weapons and an examination elite: the most economically advanced society of its era.

polities.name: Western Xia
polities.blurb: The Tangut kingdom of the Ordos and Gansu corridor, with its own script, annihilated by Genghis Khan.

polities.name: Jin Dynasty (Jurchen)
polities.blurb: The Jurchen state that drove the Song south of the Huai river, then fell to the Mongols.

polities.name: Yuan Dynasty
polities.blurb: Kublai Khan's Mongol dynasty ruling all of China from the city that became Beijing, the China Marco Polo described.

polities.name: Ming Dynasty
polities.blurb: The dynasty of the Forbidden City and Zheng He's treasure fleets, which then turned inward behind a rebuilt Great Wall.

polities.name: Qing Dynasty
polities.blurb: The Manchu dynasty that doubled China's territory, then spent the nineteenth century besieged by rebellion and foreign powers.

polities.name: China (Republic & PRC)
polities.blurb: Republic, warlords, war and revolution, then the People's Republic from 1949, today the world's second largest economy.

polities.name: Germanic Tribes
polities.blurb: The peoples beyond the Rhine and Danube whom Rome traded with, fought and finally could not hold back.

polities.name: Avar Khaganate
polities.blurb: Steppe horsemen who ruled the Carpathian basin for two and a half centuries until Charlemagne broke their power.

polities.name: Bulgarian Empire
polities.blurb: Byzantium's great Balkan rival, which gave the Slavs the Cyrillic alphabet before the Ottomans absorbed it.

polities.name: Scandinavian Kingdoms
polities.blurb: Denmark, Norway and Sweden coalesced from the Viking age, raiding and settling from Dublin to Kyiv.

polities.name: East Francia
polities.blurb: The eastern third of the Frankish partition, which grew into the German kingdom and then the Holy Roman Empire.

polities.name: Kievan Rus'
polities.blurb: The river-trade federation of Norse princes and Slavic cities that took Christianity from Byzantium, destroyed by the Mongols.

polities.name: Holy Roman Empire
polities.blurb: A loose federation of German and Italian lands under an elected emperor, more durable than centralised, dissolved by Napoleon.

polities.name: Kingdom of Hungary
polities.blurb: Founded by Stephen I on the Avars' old plain, a bulwark kingdom that endured Mongols, Ottomans and Habsburg rule.

polities.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
polities.blurb: A Slavic kingdom inside the Holy Roman Empire, birthplace of the Hussite revolt and later a Habsburg crown land.

polities.name: Serbian Empire
polities.blurb: A short-lived Balkan power at its height under Dušan, broken at Kosovo and after.

polities.name: Teutonic Order State
polities.blurb: A crusading order that conquered and ruled the Baltic coast until Poland-Lithuania broke it.

polities.name: Muscovy & Tsardom of Russia
polities.blurb: A minor principality that outmanoeuvred rivals under Mongol overlordship, then expanded east across Siberia at astonishing speed.

polities.name: Switzerland
polities.blurb: A confederation of cantons that turned mountain terrain and neutrality into seven centuries of independence.

polities.name: Poland-Lithuania
polities.blurb: A vast elective commonwealth of two nations, with an unusually powerful nobility, partitioned out of existence by its neighbours.

polities.name: Kalmar Union
polities.blurb: Denmark, Norway and Sweden under one crown, dissolved when Gustav Vasa took Sweden out.

polities.name: Sweden
polities.blurb: A Baltic great power in the seventeenth century, neutral and prosperous in the twentieth.

polities.name: Kingdom of Prussia
polities.blurb: A militarised state on poor soil that out-organised its neighbours and unified Germany around itself.

polities.name: Russian Empire
polities.blurb: Peter the Great's westernised empire, spanning eleven time zones from Warsaw to the Pacific by the nineteenth century.

polities.name: Austria-Hungary
polities.blurb: The Habsburg dual monarchy of a dozen nationalities, dissolved by defeat in 1918.

polities.name: Germany
polities.blurb: Unified under Prussia in 1871, twice defeated and divided in the twentieth century, reunified in 1990.

polities.name: Czechoslovakia
polities.blurb: Created from Habsburg lands, occupied, restored, then peacefully split in two.

polities.name: Yugoslavia
polities.blurb: A union of south Slavic peoples that held together under Tito and broke apart in war after him.

polities.name: Soviet Union
polities.blurb: The world's first communist state and one pole of the Cold War, dissolved into fifteen republics in 1991.

polities.name: Russian Federation
polities.blurb: The largest successor state of the Soviet Union and the largest country on earth by area.

polities.name: Celtic Tribes
polities.blurb: The Iron Age peoples of Gaul, Iberia and Britain, organised in shifting tribal confederations rather than states.

polities.name: Roman Gaul & Britannia
polities.blurb: Caesar's conquests brought Gaul, and later Britain, into the Roman world of roads, villas and Latin for five centuries.

polities.name: Visigothic Kingdom
polities.blurb: Gothic rulers of Iberia for three centuries, swept away by the Umayyad landing at Gibraltar.

polities.name: Frankish Kingdom
polities.blurb: The Germanic kingdom that filled Rome's western vacuum, peaking under Charlemagne before partition among his grandsons.

polities.name: Wessex & Anglo-Saxon England
polities.blurb: The West Saxon kingdom that outlasted the Viking invasions and unified the English under Alfred's heirs.

polities.name: Al-Andalus
polities.blurb: Muslim Iberia, at its height the most urbane corner of western Europe, shrinking over centuries of Reconquista until Granada fell.

polities.name: Kingdom of England
polities.blurb: From Æthelstan to the Act of Union: conquest by Normandy, the Magna Carta, the Tudors and a rising navy.

polities.name: Kingdom of France
polities.blurb: The Capetian line and its successors built Europe's model centralised monarchy, ended by the Revolution.

polities.name: Portugal
polities.blurb: A small Atlantic kingdom that opened the sea routes to Africa, India and Brazil, and kept its independence beside a larger neighbour.

polities.name: Spain
polities.blurb: The union of Castile and Aragon that built the first empire on which the sun never set, funded by American silver.

polities.name: Dutch Republic & Netherlands
polities.blurb: Seven rebel provinces that became the seventeenth century's leading trading power, then a constitutional monarchy.

polities.name: United Kingdom
polities.blurb: The union of England and Scotland that industrialised first and ran the largest empire in history at its Victorian peak.

polities.name: France
polities.blurb: Republic, empire and republic again. Through five constitutions France remained a first-rank European power.

polities.name: Ireland
polities.blurb: Independent after a war and a treaty that partitioned the island.

polities.name: Sumer
polities.blurb: The earliest urban civilisation, a patchwork of rival city-states in southern Mesopotamia that produced writing, the wheel and codified law.

polities.name: Elam
polities.blurb: The civilisation of the Iranian southwest, contemporary with Sumer and outlasting it by two thousand years.

polities.name: Akkadian Empire
polities.blurb: Sargon's unification of the Sumerian city-states, often counted as the first empire.

polities.name: Third Dynasty of Ur
polities.blurb: A Sumerian renaissance under the kings who built the great ziggurat of Ur and ran history's most documented bureaucracy.

polities.name: Old Babylonian Empire
polities.blurb: Babylon's first ascendancy, remembered above all for Hammurabi and his law stele.

polities.name: Kassite Babylonia
polities.blurb: Babylonia's longest dynasty, foreign-born kings who governed quietly for four centuries between louder empires.

polities.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
polities.blurb: The iron-age superpower of the Near East, ruling by army and archive from the Nile to the Zagros, hated and imitated in equal measure.

polities.name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
polities.blurb: Nebuchadnezzar's brief, brilliant Babylon, of the hanging gardens and the Judean exile, taken by Cyrus without a siege.

polities.name: Achaemenid Empire
polities.blurb: The first empire to span three continents, ruling from the Indus to the Aegean through satraps and a royal road network.

polities.name: Seleucid Empire
polities.blurb: The largest fragment of Alexander's conquests, a Greek-ruled state stretching from Anatolia toward the Indus.

polities.name: Parthian Empire
polities.blurb: Iran's horse-archer empire, Rome's stubborn eastern equal for three centuries and the middleman of the Silk Road.

polities.name: Sasanian Empire
polities.blurb: The last pre-Islamic Persian empire, Zoroastrian and centralised, exhausted by Byzantine wars just before the Arab conquest.

polities.name: Abbasid Caliphate
polities.blurb: The caliphate of Baghdad's golden age, when the House of Wisdom translated the world's learning into Arabic, ended by the Mongol sack.

polities.name: Buyid Dynasty
polities.blurb: Shia Iranian rulers who held Baghdad and kept the Abbasid caliph as a figurehead.

polities.name: Great Seljuk Empire
polities.blurb: Turkic nomads who took Persia and Baghdad, beat Byzantium at Manzikert and provoked the First Crusade.

polities.name: Ilkhanate
polities.blurb: The Mongol khanate of Persia, whose rulers converted to Islam and patronised a flowering of Persian art and history writing.

polities.name: Safavid Empire
polities.blurb: The dynasty that made Iran Shia and made Isfahan half the world, in the proverb of the time.

polities.name: Qajar Iran
polities.blurb: Iran squeezed between Russian and British empires, keeping formal independence while losing territory and concessions.

polities.name: Iran
polities.blurb: The Pahlavi monarchy and, since 1979, the Islamic Republic.

polities.name: Gojoseon
polities.blurb: The first Korean kingdom, its legendary founding dated to 2333 BCE but its verifiable history beginning much later, ended by Han conquest.

polities.name: Three Kingdoms of Korea
polities.blurb: Goguryeo, Baekje and Silla contended for the peninsula for seven centuries until Silla won with Tang help.

polities.name: Kofun & Yamato Japan
polities.blurb: The age of great keyhole tombs and the first Japanese state, importing writing and Buddhism through Korea.

polities.name: Unified Silla
polities.blurb: The first unification of most of Korea, a Buddhist golden age centred on Gyeongju.

polities.name: Balhae
polities.blurb: A Goguryeo successor state in Manchuria and northern Korea, called the flourishing land in the east.

polities.name: Heian Japan
polities.blurb: Four centuries of courtly rule from Kyoto, the world of the Tale of Genji, ending as warrior clans took power.

polities.name: Goryeo
polities.blurb: The dynasty that gave Korea its Western name, printer of the Tripitaka Koreana and inventor of metal movable type.

polities.name: Kamakura Shogunate
polities.blurb: Japan's first shogunate, which twice turned back Kublai Khan's invasion fleets with the help of storms named kamikaze.

polities.name: Ainu Lands
polities.blurb: The Ainu homeland across Hokkaido and Sakhalin, absorbed into Japan during the Meiji period.

polities.name: Ashikaga Shogunate
polities.blurb: A weak shogunate whose collapse into the Warring States era coincided with Zen, the tea ceremony and the first Europeans.

polities.name: Joseon
polities.blurb: Five centuries of Confucian monarchy that created the hangul alphabet and weathered invasions from both Japan and the Manchus.

polities.name: Ryukyu Kingdom
polities.blurb: An island kingdom that traded between Japan, China and Southeast Asia before Japan annexed it.

polities.name: Sengoku Period
polities.blurb: A century of warring domains in Japan, ended by three successive unifiers and the arrival of firearms.

polities.name: Tokugawa Shogunate
polities.blurb: Two and a half centuries of enforced peace and near-closed borders, with Edo growing into a city of a million.

polities.name: Japan
polities.blurb: From the Meiji Restoration through empire, defeat and reconstruction to the world's fourth largest economy.

polities.name: Korea
polities.blurb: The peninsula divided since 1945 into two states, the South an industrial democracy, the North a dynastic autocracy.

polities.name: Minoan Civilisation
polities.blurb: Europe's first literate civilisation, palace towns on Crete trading across the Aegean until eruption, earthquake and Mycenaean takeover.

polities.name: Mycenaean Greece
polities.blurb: The palace kingdoms of Homer's heroes, undone in the general collapse of the Bronze Age eastern Mediterranean.

polities.name: Carthage
polities.blurb: The Phoenician colony that became the western Mediterranean's naval power, destroyed by Rome after three wars.

polities.name: Greek City-States
polities.blurb: Athens, Sparta and hundreds of rivals invented citizenship, drama, philosophy and history writing between their wars.

polities.name: Roman Republic
polities.blurb: The city-state that conquered the Mediterranean under an elected magistracy before collapsing into one-man rule.

polities.name: Kingdom of Macedon
polities.blurb: Philip II mastered Greece and his son Alexander conquered Persia to the Indus, scattering Greek culture across three continents.

polities.name: Roman Empire
polities.blurb: The Mediterranean's single largest and longest shadow, an empire of roads, law and legions ringing the entire sea.

polities.name: Western Roman Empire
polities.blurb: The western half of the divided empire, dismantled within a century by migrating peoples and its own generals.

polities.name: Byzantine Empire
polities.blurb: The eastern Roman state that outlived the west by a thousand years, Greek-speaking and Christian, anchored on Constantinople.

polities.name: Lombard Kingdom
polities.blurb: Germanic rulers of most of Italy after Byzantium's brief reconquest, ended by Charlemagne.

polities.name: Republic of Venice
polities.blurb: A lagoon city that ran the eastern Mediterranean's trade for centuries, its arsenal the largest industrial site in Europe.

polities.name: Papal States
polities.blurb: The pope's temporal kingdom across central Italy, a fixture of European politics for eleven centuries until Italian unification.

polities.name: Norman Kingdom of Sicily
polities.blurb: Norman adventurers built a Latin, Greek and Arabic kingdom in the central Mediterranean.

polities.name: Greece
polities.blurb: The first new state carved from the Ottoman Empire, recognised after a decade of revolutionary war.

polities.name: Italy
polities.blurb: The peninsula's patchwork of kingdoms and duchies unified under Piedmont, completed when Rome fell in 1870.

polities.name: Canaanite & Phoenician Cities
polities.blurb: The merchant cities of the Levant coast, Byblos to Tyre, who spread the alphabet along their sea lanes.

polities.name: Hittite Empire
polities.blurb: The Anatolian great power that fought Egypt to a standstill at Kadesh and signed history's first surviving peace treaty.

polities.name: Mitanni
polities.blurb: A Hurrian kingdom of northern Mesopotamia and Syria, a fourth player among the Bronze Age great powers until Assyria absorbed it.

polities.name: Phrygia
polities.blurb: An Anatolian kingdom remembered through the legends of Midas and the Gordian knot.

polities.name: Israel & Judah
polities.blurb: The Hebrew kingdoms of the southern Levant, whose scriptures long outlived the states themselves.

polities.name: Urartu
polities.blurb: A highland kingdom around Lake Van, Assyria's most persistent northern rival.

polities.name: Kingdom of Lydia
polities.blurb: An Anatolian kingdom credited with minting the first true coinage, its last king Croesus a proverb for wealth.

polities.name: Kingdom of Armenia
polities.blurb: A highland kingdom between Rome and Persia, the first state to adopt Christianity as its official religion.

polities.name: Nabataean Kingdom
polities.blurb: Caravan traders who cut Petra from rock and controlled the incense route until Rome annexed them.

polities.name: Ghassanids & Lakhmids
polities.blurb: Arab client kingdoms on the desert frontier, one serving Byzantium and the other Persia.

polities.name: Palmyrene Empire
polities.blurb: Zenobia's desert city briefly seized Egypt and Anatolia from a distracted Rome, then was erased by it.

polities.name: Rashidun Caliphate
polities.blurb: The first four caliphs after Muhammad, under whom Arab armies took the Levant, Egypt and Persia within a generation.

polities.name: Umayyad Caliphate
polities.blurb: The dynasty that carried Islam from the Atlantic to the Indus, the largest empire the world had yet seen.

polities.name: Bagratid Armenia
polities.blurb: A restored Armenian kingdom whose capital Ani was called the city of a thousand and one churches.

polities.name: Sultanate of Rum
polities.blurb: The Seljuk successor state in Anatolia that turkified Asia Minor, ancestor of the beyliks from which the Ottomans rose.

polities.name: Crusader States
polities.blurb: Latin Christian statelets planted in the Levant by the First Crusade, ending when Acre fell to the Mamluks.

polities.name: Ottoman Empire
polities.blurb: The Turkish empire that took Constantinople and ruled the eastern Mediterranean, the Balkans and the Hejaz for six centuries.

polities.name: Turkey
polities.blurb: Atatürk's secular republic built from the Ottoman core after the empire's partition.

polities.name: Old Kingdom Egypt
polities.blurb: The pyramid-building age of Egypt, when the state along the Nile reached its first peak of centralised power.

polities.name: Middle Kingdom Egypt
polities.blurb: Egypt reunified after a century of fragmentation, a classical age of literature and administration.

polities.name: New Kingdom Egypt
polities.blurb: Egypt's imperial era under rulers like Thutmose III and Ramesses II, projecting power into the Levant and Nubia.

polities.name: Third Intermediate Period
polities.blurb: Egypt divided among rival dynasties, including a century of rule by the Kushite kings of the south.

polities.name: Late Period Egypt
polities.blurb: The last native dynasties, alternating with Persian rule, before Alexander took Egypt without a fight.

polities.name: Ptolemaic Egypt
polities.blurb: The Greek dynasty of Alexander's general Ptolemy, ending with Cleopatra. Alexandria was the ancient world's great library city.

polities.name: Numidia & Mauretania
polities.blurb: Berber kingdoms of the Maghreb that allied with and against Rome before annexation.

polities.name: Roman Egypt
polities.blurb: Rome's breadbasket province, then Byzantine, until the Arab conquest carried it into a different world.

polities.name: Fatimid Caliphate
polities.blurb: An Ismaili Shia caliphate that founded Cairo and ruled from Tunisia to Syria at its height.

polities.name: Almoravid Empire
polities.blurb: Berber reformers from the Sahara who united Morocco and rescued Muslim Spain from the Reconquista.

polities.name: Almohad Caliphate
polities.blurb: Their successors ruled from Iberia to Libya before losing Spain at Las Navas de Tolosa.

polities.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
polities.blurb: Saladin's dynasty, which retook Jerusalem from the crusaders and ruled Egypt and Syria.

polities.name: Hafsid & Zayyanid Maghreb
polities.blurb: Successor dynasties of the Almohads in Tunisia and Algeria, later Ottoman regencies.

polities.name: Mamluk Sultanate
polities.blurb: A regime of slave-soldiers who stopped the Mongols at Ain Jalut and ruled Egypt and Syria until the Ottomans took Cairo.

polities.name: Ottoman & Khedival Egypt
polities.blurb: Egypt under Ottoman rule and then Muhammad Ali's ambitious dynasty, ending in British occupation.

polities.name: Morocco
polities.blurb: The Alaouite dynasty has ruled Morocco from the seventeenth century through a French protectorate to the present kingdom.

polities.name: Egypt
polities.blurb: Nominal independence from Britain in 1922, full sovereignty after 1952, and the Arab world's most populous state.

polities.name: New Guinea Highland Societies
polities.blurb: Among the world's earliest agriculturalists at Kuk Swamp, in valleys unknown to outsiders until the 1930s.

polities.name: Lapita Culture
polities.blurb: Seafaring pottery-makers who carried people, pigs and languages from Near Oceania out into the remote Pacific.

polities.name: Polynesian Expansion
polities.blurb: The longest voyages of the pre-modern world, settling islands from Samoa to Hawaiʻi, Rapa Nui and finally Aotearoa by double-hulled canoe.

polities.name: Fijian & Samoan Chiefdoms
polities.blurb: Rival chiefdoms of western Polynesia and Melanesia, linked by voyaging, marriage and war.

polities.name: Tuʻi Tonga Empire
polities.blurb: A Tongan maritime chiefdom whose influence and tribute networks reached across a wide arc of the central Pacific.

polities.name: Māori Iwi
polities.blurb: The tribal nations of Aotearoa New Zealand, from first settlement to the Treaty of Waitangi.

polities.name: Kingdom of Hawaiʻi
polities.blurb: Kamehameha I unified the islands into a recognised monarchy that lasted until a planter-led coup backed by American interests.

polities.name: New Zealand
polities.blurb: Founded on the Treaty of Waitangi, the first country to give women the vote.

polities.name: Australia
polities.blurb: The federated Commonwealth of six British colonies, on a continent inhabited by Aboriginal peoples for tens of millennia before 1788.

polities.name: Indus Valley Civilisation
polities.blurb: Planned brick cities with sewers and standard weights across the Indus basin, whose script is still undeciphered.

polities.name: Vedic Kingdoms
polities.blurb: The age of the Vedas: pastoral clans of the northwest settling the Ganges plain and becoming kingdoms.

polities.name: Mahajanapadas
polities.blurb: Sixteen great states of the Ganges plain, the world the Buddha and Mahavira taught in, gradually swallowed by Magadha.

polities.name: Maurya Empire
polities.blurb: The first state to unify most of the Indian subcontinent, remembered above all for Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism.

polities.name: Satavahana Dynasty
polities.blurb: The Deccan dynasty that bridged north and south India and patronised early Buddhist monuments like Amaravati.

polities.name: Pallavas & Chalukyas
polities.blurb: Rival southern dynasties whose rock-cut temples set the pattern for South Indian architecture.

polities.name: Gupta Empire
polities.blurb: North India's classical age: Kalidasa's poetry, the zero, and astronomy that travelled west through Arabic translation.

polities.name: Pala Empire
polities.blurb: Bengal's Buddhist dynasty, patron of Nalanda and the last great sponsor of Indian Buddhism.

polities.name: Rashtrakuta Dynasty
polities.blurb: Deccan emperors who carved the Kailasa temple from a single rock and were praised by Arab travellers.

polities.name: Chola Empire
polities.blurb: The Tamil maritime empire that raided Srivijaya across the Bay of Bengal and built the great temples of the Kaveri delta.

polities.name: Delhi Sultanate
polities.blurb: Five successive Turko-Afghan dynasties ruling from Delhi, which twice repelled Mongol invasions of India.

polities.name: Vijayanagara Empire
polities.blurb: The last great Hindu empire of the south, its capital described by visitors as among the largest cities in the world.

polities.name: Bengal Sultanate
polities.blurb: An independent, wealthy delta sultanate that traded with China and was absorbed by the Mughals.

polities.name: Mughal Empire
polities.blurb: Babur's Timurid dynasty in India, at its peak the richest empire on earth, builder of the Taj Mahal.

polities.name: Maratha Confederacy
polities.blurb: Shivaji's Hindu warrior state that broke Mughal power across the subcontinent before losing three wars to the British.

polities.name: British India
polities.blurb: Company rule and then the Crown Raj, the centrepiece of the British Empire, ending in independence and Partition.

polities.name: Sikh Empire
polities.blurb: Ranjit Singh's Punjab state, the last major Indian power to fall to the British.

polities.name: India
polities.blurb: The world's largest democracy and, since 2023, its most populous country.

polities.name: Đông Sơn Culture
polities.blurb: Bronze-drum makers of the Red River delta, the culture behind the legendary first Vietnamese kingdoms.

polities.name: Funan
polities.blurb: The Mekong delta's first major polity, an Indian Ocean trading state known mostly through Chinese envoys' reports.

polities.name: Champa
polities.blurb: A Hindu then Muslim maritime kingdom on the Vietnamese coast, absorbed over centuries by Dai Viet.

polities.name: Srivijaya
polities.blurb: The Sumatran thalassocracy that controlled the Malacca and Sunda straits, a great centre of Buddhist learning.

polities.name: Khmer Empire
polities.nameNative: ចក្រភពខ្មែរ
polities.blurb: The empire of Angkor, whose temple-city was the largest urban complex of the pre-industrial world.

polities.name: Pagan Kingdom
polities.blurb: The first unification of the lands that became Myanmar, its plain still crowded with thousands of brick temples.

polities.name: Đại Việt
polities.blurb: Vietnam independent of China after a millennium, repelling Song, Mongol and Ming invasions while expanding south.

polities.name: Majapahit
polities.blurb: The Javanese empire whose claimed reach across the archipelago later inspired the idea of Indonesia itself.

polities.name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
polities.blurb: The Siamese kingdom whose cosmopolitan island capital hosted Persian, Japanese and French quarters before Burmese armies burned it.

polities.name: Lan Xang
polities.blurb: The kingdom of a million elephants, ancestor of modern Laos.

polities.name: Malacca Sultanate
polities.blurb: The strait's great entrepôt and a centre of Islam's spread through the archipelago, taken by Portugal in 1511.

polities.name: Toungoo & Konbaung Burma
polities.blurb: Burmese dynasties that built Southeast Asia's largest empire, then lost three wars to Britain.

polities.name: Philippines
polities.blurb: Spanish for three centuries, American for four decades, independent since 1946.

polities.name: Dutch East Indies
polities.blurb: Three centuries of Dutch company and state rule over the spice archipelago.

polities.name: Siam / Thailand
polities.blurb: The Chakri dynasty's kingdom, the one state in Southeast Asia never colonised.

polities.name: Indonesia
polities.blurb: The archipelago republic proclaimed in 1945, today the world's fourth most populous country.

polities.name: Kingdom of Kerma
polities.blurb: The first Nubian kingdom, a rival to Egypt on the upper Nile with monumental mud-brick architecture of its own.

polities.name: Egyptian Nubia
polities.blurb: Nubia under New Kingdom viceroys, its gold funding Egypt's imperial age.

polities.name: Nok Culture
polities.blurb: West Africa's earliest known iron-working society, famous for its terracotta heads.

polities.name: Kingdom of Kush
polities.blurb: The Nubian kingdom that conquered and briefly ruled Egypt itself, then flourished at Meroë as an iron-working power for centuries.

polities.name: Kingdom of Aksum
polities.blurb: A Red Sea trading empire that minted its own coins and adopted Christianity in the fourth century, among the first states to do so.

polities.name: Ghana Empire
polities.blurb: The first great Sahel trading empire, taxing the gold and salt caravans between the forest and the Sahara.

polities.name: Kanem-Bornu Empire
polities.blurb: A Saharan empire around Lake Chad that endured under one dynastic tradition for over a thousand years.

polities.name: Swahili City-States
polities.blurb: Coral-stone trading towns from Mogadishu to Sofala that linked Africa to India and China.

polities.name: Kingdom of Benin
polities.blurb: A forest kingdom in present-day Nigeria famous for its bronze casting, sacked by a British expedition in 1897.

polities.name: Great Zimbabwe
polities.blurb: The stone-walled capital of a Shona kingdom grown rich on gold and Indian Ocean trade through Kilwa.

polities.name: Mali Empire
polities.blurb: Sundiata's empire on the upper Niger. Mansa Musa's gold-laden pilgrimage to Mecca made it a byword for wealth across the old world.

polities.name: Ethiopian Empire
polities.blurb: The Solomonic dynasty's Christian highland empire, the one African state to defeat a European coloniser at Adwa in 1896.

polities.name: Oyo Empire
polities.blurb: A Yoruba cavalry empire that dominated the Bight of Benin and constrained its own kings by council.

polities.name: Buganda
polities.blurb: A centralised lakeside kingdom in the Great Lakes, later the core of colonial Uganda.

polities.name: Kingdom of Kongo
polities.blurb: A central African kingdom that exchanged embassies with Portugal and the Vatican, then was hollowed out by the slave trade.

polities.name: Songhai Empire
polities.blurb: The largest state in West African history, with Timbuktu as its scholarly centre, broken by a Moroccan musket army.

polities.name: Funj Sultanate
polities.blurb: The Islamic sultanate of the upper Nile between Egypt and Ethiopia.

polities.name: Ashanti Empire
polities.blurb: A gold-rich Akan empire whose golden stool embodied the nation, absorbed into British Gold Coast after five wars.

polities.name: Zulu Kingdom
polities.blurb: Shaka's military revolution reshaped southern Africa and defeated a British column at Isandlwana.

polities.name: South Africa
polities.blurb: The union of British colonies and Boer republics, under apartheid from 1948 until the 1994 elections.

polities.name: Nigeria
polities.blurb: Africa's most populous country, assembled from Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo lands under British rule.
